newsitem.title: USA: U.S. might ease Latam arms policy - officials.
newsitem.headline: U.S. might ease Latam arms policy - officials.

text.p: The outgoing U.S. secretaries of state and defence have urged President Bill Clinton to change policy and consider the sale of high tech arms to Latin America on a case-by-case basis, U.S. officials said on Wednesday.

Such a shift, proposed in a memo to the White House by departing Secretary of State Warren Christopher and Defence Secretary William Perry, would end a virtual ban on sales of frontline fighter jets and other such arms to Latin America.

"They did sign a memo and send it to the White House within the past few weeks," Navy Cmdr. Joe March, a Defense Department spokesman, told Reuters in response to questions. "The subject was the consideration of arms sales to Latin America on a case-by-case basis."

Christopher has in the past publicly opposed such an easing of the ban because he believed it might fuel an arms race, but other U.S. officials said privately on Wednesday that he had been persuaded by Perry that the time had come for change because all Latin American nations except Cuba were now democracies.
Clinton is expected to visit Latin America early this year, perhaps in March, and a new policy could be in place by then.

Retiring Republican Sen. William Cohen of Maine, who has been nominated by Clinton to replace Perry, earlier signed a letter with 39 other senators urging the White House to ease the policy on a case-by-case basis. Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright's position on the issue is not known.
